newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN Council mildly raps Libya on flight ban.
newsitem.headline: UN Council mildly raps Libya on flight ban.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council said on Tuesday that Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi violated sanctions by flying to Niger and Nigeria earlier this month.

In a statement, the council noted "with concern" reports that Libyan-registered aircraft flew to Niger on May 8 and return to Libya from Nigeria on May 10 in violation of sanctions. The mildly-worded statement was a compromise mainly between the United States and Egypt.
The council said its Libya sanctions committee would follow up the issue directly with envoys from Libya, Niger and Nigeria.

A flotilla of four Libyan aircraft recently flew Gaddafi and others to Niger and Nigeria, and back to Libya, despite the U.N. ban. Libya said Gaddafi visited the West African countries for prayers marking the Muslim New Year as head of the Islamic Popular Leadership, an organization he created in 1989.

Libya has been subject to mandatory U.N. sanctions since 1992, including a ban on international flights and an arms embargo, for failing to extradite two men wanted by Britain and the United States in the 1988 mid-air bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, which killed 270 people.
Several countries said the flights were for religious purposes and should be allowed, even though Libya had not sought permission in advance.
